newsitem.title: USA: Nice chairman says EPS view "challenging".
newsitem.headline: Nice chairman says EPS view "challenging".

text.p: The chairman of Israel's Nice Systems Ltd said Wednesday an analyst's estimates for 1997 and 1998 earnings per share were "challenging but achievable."

Asked if he was comfortable with projections by Josephthal Lyon and Ross analyst Robert Goldman of $1.27 per share this year and $1.67 in 1998, chairman David Arzi told Reuters, "I would say comfortable is not a good word, but I think it's challenging but achievable."
Arzi was speaking at a Josephthal Lyon and Ross conference on Israeli companies.
Nice, a maker of digital systems that record and retrieve conversations, had income of $2.15 million, or $0.28 a share, on revenues of $13.3 million in the first quarter of 1997.
Income for 1996 was $5.2 million, or $0.70 a share, on revenues of $39.8 million.
Arzi also said the planned purchase of Canada's Dees Communications would widen Nice's presence in North America.

Nice said Thursday it had signed a letter of intent to buy Dees for $8 million in cash and up to 500,000 in ordinary shares. Dees provides automated call center monitoring solutions and is a preferred vendor to Northern Telecom Ltd, Arzi said.
A definitive agreement for the purchase is to be completed in two months.
The acquisition will triple the number of Nice sales personnel in North America. Nice has 40 to 50 salespeople in the region, he said.
Arzi described the purchase as "low risk," adding that it puts Nice "in a potentially leading position in this market."
